text:
Alex: Quick sync — noticed the post-launch content spike last night but the dashboard is showing a weird attribution split. 50% 'organic' leads with no utm_source, then a small bucket tagged as 'email' that doesn't match the send we did. Anyone else seeing this?
Rachael: I pulled the lead table and saw duplicates coming from the inbound webhook. looks like some leads hit twice during the 2m window after the launch burst. digging now. :mag_right:
Mike: @Rachael can you confirm whether the webhook dedupe is using `external_id` or email? We rely on `external_id` for a lot of partners.
Rachael: it's currently email. partner sends sometimes omit email => two rows. switching to `external_id` would help but need to confirm partner payload.
Jess: For context, the launch-post creative had two shortened links (one for mobile CTA and one for desktop). Could the UTM parameters differ between them? I remember we forgot to unify `utm_content`.
Sam: I flagged that in the messaging doc — we intentionally used `utm_content=hero` vs `utm_content=hero_alt` to run A/B on copy. might explain split.
Alex: Ok — so multiple causes: webhook dedupe by email + deliberate UTM variant. Can we get a short actionable plan in this thread? Want to avoid a messy KPI number in Monday review.
Rachael: Plan: 1) temporary dedupe patch on ingestion to collapse by `external_id` if present, else email (2) canonicalize UTMs for baseline reporting — roll up `utm_content` variants under `hero` for last 48h (3) reprocess the inbound lead batch for the launch window to update source attribution. I can own 1 and 3.
Mike: I'll coordinate with Infra to deploy the ingestion patch. ETA today EOD. tagging @growth-bot to run the reprocess job after Rachael's script is ready.
growth-bot: scheduled job queued: `reprocess_inbound_leads --from 2026-03-20T22:00Z --to 2026-03-21T02:00Z` — will run once artifact is uploaded. :white_check_mark:
Jess: For the dashboards — can we add a temporary metric called `attribution_confidence` that flags leads with ambiguous UTMs or missing external_id? would make the weekly review easier to interpret.
Rachael: good idea. I can add a derived boolean and a small note for the dashboard header.
Alex: Thanks. Also, heads-up for webinar folks: the launch traffic fed the webinar signup form and we should avoid double-emailing those contacts. Jess, can your team add a dedupe check to the follow-up drip?
Jess: yes — adding check `if contact.source == 'launch_post' && contacted_in_24h then skip` into the workflow. will push a small rule today.
Mike: After the ingestion fix and reprocess, can someone run the standard sanity SQL and paste results here? quick query I use:
```
SELECT source, count(*) as leads, count(DISTINCT email) as unique_emails
FROM inbound_leads
WHERE created_at BETWEEN '2026-03-20' AND '2026-03-21'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY leads DESC;
```
Rachael: will run and paste results once reprocess completes.
Sam: small ask — for future launches, can we lock `utm_source` and `utm_medium` across variants and only run `utm_content` experiments? seems like mixing source changes with content tests complicates attribution.
Alex: Agreed. Let's add that to the launch playbook. I'll draft a 1-pager with the new rule and a checklist item: "Canonicalize UTMs for baseline metrics".
Jess: putting that on the playbook now.
Rachael: reprocess finished, summary: duplicates reduced by ~18%, majority of previously-unattributed leads now roll up to `launch_post` after UTMs canonicalized. dashboard numbers look much cleaner. I'll post the final CSV to the #marketing-data S3 bucket.
Alex: Awesome — thanks everyone. We'll mark this resolved for the weekly review but include a short note on the numbers change. :memo:
